summary: WorldEntity persistentState has no declared canonical payload/workload budget. clonePlainValue() recursively owns every accepted nested table/value and enforces plain-data shape, cycles, and dense arrays, but it has no maximum nesting depth, node/entry count, aggregate string/key bytes, or total payload-work ceiling. WorldEntity.new(), register()/ownRecord(), captureState(), and demotion capture can therefore perform recursion and allocations proportional to caller-supplied accepted state size. PR #293 hardens lifecycle ownership/revision/no-execute boundaries but leaves this recursive payload-budget behavior unchanged. Follow-up should define a versioned persistent-state complexity budget, reject over-budget state before deep ownership work where practical, add depth/node/aggregate-byte boundary tests, and preserve existing in-budget state semantics.
evidence: src/shared/Reality/WorldEntity.luau: clonePlainValue() recursively walks and freezes arbitrary accepted nested plain tables; cloneState() delegates the whole persistentState graph to it without depth, node-count, aggregate-byte, or equivalent complexity limits.

WorldEntity.new(), ownRecord()/registry.register(), captureState(), and demotion transition all own or clone persistent state through that recursive path, so CPU/allocations scale with accepted caller payload size.
PR #293 changes record ownership, revision ranges, generatorVersion, and fail-closed diagnostics but does not add a persistent-state complexity/work budget.

Repository issue/PR/code search plus same-day event-name audit found no existing WorldEntity persistentState depth/size/workload-budget closure. Source-only finding: no benchmark, exploit claim, or Roblox Studio evidence is asserted.
